intro: You already know my bag and Rina's phone. Today you'll learn to say it's mine, it's hers and they're ours, to ask Whose …? about one thing or many, and to write 's and s' the right way (my friend's book, my parents' house). Warm-up: look at the things on your table. Which ones are yours?
teachingNotes: Core rule: my, your, his, her, our, their always need a thing (a noun) right after them (my bag). When the thing isn't said again, use mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs with nothing after them: This bag is mine. Typical errors: *This bag is my, *It's mine bag, *mines, and an apostrophe in yours/hers/ours/theirs (*your's, *her's). his is the same in both jobs (his bag / it's his). Don't teach its as a pronoun on its own; say it's almost never used alone.

Indonesian 'punya saya / milik saya / punyaku' = mine, while 'tas saya' = my bag. Learners translate 'Tas ini punya saya' as *This bag is my. Also stress the speaker's point of view: Budi and Sari say 'It's ours', but you, talking about them, say 'It's theirs'. yours is for one person and for a group (kamu / kalian).

Whose asks about the owner: Whose + thing + is this? / are these? (plural: are, and answer They're …). Whose is this? is fine when the thing is clear. Answer with a name + 's or with mine/yours/his/hers/ours/theirs: It's Rina's. / It's mine. / They're his. Whose and who's sound the same; who's = who is (Who's that man?). Test: if 'who is' fits, write who's. Don't teach whose in the middle of a sentence (the man whose car …).

One owner: 's (my friend's book, my sister's room). More than one owner and the word already ends in s: only ' after the s (my parents' house = mother AND father; my sisters' room = two sisters). Plurals that don't end in s (children, people, men, women) take 's: the children's toys, the women's toilet. parent's, parents and parents' all sound the same; only the writing (or the context) shows one or more. Common errors: *my parent's house for both parents, *That's the book of my friend (Indonesian 'buku teman saya'). Owner names ending in s (Agus, Dimas): accept both Agus's and Agus'; don't build questions on them.

Explain jargon in plain Indonesian: noun = kata benda (thing, person, place); plural = more than one; apostrophe = the small mark '. If the learner asks about 'of': for people and animals English uses 's; don't go into 'of' with things (the name of the street) in this lesson.

Limits: present simple, be, present continuous, can, there is/are and was/were only. No past simple, no will, no present perfect. Don't teach double possessives (a friend of mine); if asked, call it a phrase to remember.

keyPoints.title: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs
keyPoints.explanation: my, your, his, her, our, their need a thing right after them (my bag). When the thing isn't said again, use mine, yours, his, hers, ours or theirs with nothing after: This bag is mine, not 'This bag is my'. his stays his. No apostrophe and no extra s: yours (not your's), mine (not mines).

id.title: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs
id.explanation: my, your, his, her, our, their harus langsung diikuti benda (my bag). Kalau bendanya tidak disebut lagi, pakai mine, yours, his, hers, ours atau theirs tanpa kata apa pun sesudahnya: This bag is mine, bukan 'This bag is my'. his tetap his. Tanpa apostrof dan tanpa s tambahan: yours (bukan your's), mine (bukan mines).

keyPoints.title: Whose …?
keyPoints.explanation: Ask about the owner with Whose + thing + is this? (one thing) or are these? (more than one). Answer with a name + 's or with mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs: It's Rina's. / They're mine. whose and who's sound the same, but who's = who is.

examples.en: Whose phone is this? — It's Rina's.
Whose glasses are these? — They're his.

examples.id: Siapa manajermu? — Pak Hasan. (who's = who is)

id.title: Whose …?
id.explanation: Tanyakan pemiliknya dengan Whose + benda + is this? (satu benda) atau are these? (lebih dari satu). Jawab dengan nama + 's atau dengan mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs: It's Rina's. / They're mine. whose dan who's bunyinya sama, tapi who's = who is.

keyPoints.title: 's and s'
keyPoints.explanation: One owner: add 's (my friend's book). More than one owner, and the word already ends in s: add only ' (my parents' house = your mother and father). Words for more than one that don't end in s (children, people, men, women) take 's: the children's toys. The owner always comes first: my friend's book, not 'the book of my friend'.

examples.en: My friend's book is on the table.
examples.id: Buku teman saya ada di meja. (satu teman)

examples.en: My parents' house is in Bandung.
examples.id: Rumah orang tua saya di Bandung. (ayah dan ibu)

examples.en: The children's toys are on the floor.

id.title: 's dan s'
id.explanation: Satu pemilik: tambahkan 's (my friend's book). Lebih dari satu pemilik dan katanya sudah berakhiran s: tambahkan ' saja (my parents' house = ayah dan ibumu). Kata 'lebih dari satu' yang tidak berakhiran s (children, people, men, women) memakai 's: the children's toys. Pemilik selalu di depan: my friend's book, bukan 'the book of my friend'.

assessment.prompt: Complete the second sentence with one word so it means the same: Is this your helmet? → Is this helmet ___?
assessment.rubric: Correct: yours. 'your' = 10 (your needs a thing after it). 'your's' = 60 (no apostrophe in yours). 'you' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Pak Hasan and Bu Ani point at a white car and say, 'That's our car.' You tell a friend about it. Complete with mine, yours, his, hers, ours or theirs: The white car is ___.
assessment.rubric: Correct: theirs (you are talking about them). 'ours' = 30 (that's what they say, not you). 'their' = 30 (needs a thing after it). 'their's' = 70 (spelling).

assessment.prompt: You see two helmets on a chair in the office. Write a question with Whose to find out who they belong to.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Whose helmets are these? 'Whose helmets is this' = 60 (one/many mix). 'Who's helmets are these' = 50 (who's = who is). 'Whose is helmets these' = 30. 'Who has these helmets' = 20 (doesn't use whose).

assessment.prompt: Listen to the question. The bag belongs to Sari. Answer with a short sentence. Use mine, yours, his, hers, ours or theirs.
assessment.rubric: Correct: It's hers. 'It's her bag' or 'It's Sari's' = 70 (right, but not one of the given words). 'It's her' = 20. 'It's his' = 20 (Sari is a woman). 'It's her's' = 70 (spelling).

assessment.prompt: Complete with Whose or Who's: ___ that woman with Pak Hasan? — She's his wife.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Who's (= Who is: the question asks who the woman is, not who owns something). 'Whose' = 0. 'Who' = 40 (missing is).

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: My grandmother and grandfather live in Surabaya. Every Lebaran we stay at my ___ house.
assessment.rubric: Correct: grandparents' (two owners, word already ends in s). 'grandparent's' = 50 (means one grandparent). 'grandparents' without ' = 60. 'grandparents's' = 70. 'grandmother's' = 40 (only one of them).

assessment.prompt: Translate into English: Ini motor kakak laki-laki saya. (Kakak saya hanya satu.)
acceptableAnswers: this is my older brother's motorbike
this is my older brother's motorcycle
this is my big brother's motorbike
this is my big brother's motorcycle
assessment.rubric: Correct: This is my (older) brother's motorbike. 'the motorbike of my brother' = 40 (Indonesian word order). 'my brother motorbike' = 50 (missing 's). 'my brothers' motorbike' = 50 (means more than one brother). Missing 'is' = 70.

blocks.text:
You know **my bag, your phone, her name**. These words (**my, your, his, her, our, their**) always need a **thing** right after them. (A *thing* here means a *noun*: the name of a thing, person or place, like *bag, car, office*.)

But often we don't say the thing again, because everyone already knows it. Then **my** can't stand alone. We use a different word, with **nothing after it**:
- my → **mine**
- your → **yours**
- his → **his** (no change)
- her → **hers**
- our → **ours**
- their → **theirs**

So: *This is **my** bag.* = *This bag is **mine**.* Not *This bag is my*.

id.text:
Kamu sudah tahu **my bag, your phone, her name**. Kata-kata ini (**my, your, his, her, our, their**) selalu harus langsung diikuti **benda**. (*Benda* di sini artinya *kata benda/noun*: nama benda, orang atau tempat, seperti *bag, car, office*.)

Tapi sering kita tidak menyebut bendanya lagi, karena semua orang sudah tahu. Saat itu **my** tidak bisa berdiri sendiri. Kita pakai kata lain, **tanpa kata apa pun sesudahnya**:
- my → **mine**
- your → **yours**
- his → **his** (tidak berubah)
- her → **hers**
- our → **ours**
- their → **theirs**

Jadi: *This is **my** bag.* = *This bag is **mine**.* Bukan *This bag is my*.

rows.en: That umbrella isn't mine. Mine is black.
rows.id: Payung itu bukan punya saya. Punya saya hitam.

rows.en: Is this coffee yours, Bu Ani?
rows.id: Kopi ini punya Ibu, Bu Ani?

rows.en: Our office is small, but theirs is big.
rows.id: Kantor kami kecil, tapi kantor mereka besar.

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap.** *Tas ini punya saya* has no word for 'thing' after *punya saya*, so learners write *This bag is my*. Remember: **punya saya / milik saya / punyaku = mine**, but **tas saya = my bag**. Three more traps:
- No apostrophe: **yours, hers, ours, theirs** (not *your's, her's*).
- No extra s on **mine** (not *mines*), and never *mine bag*.
- **yours** is for one person and for a group (*kamu* and *kalian*).

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia.** Dalam *Tas ini punya saya*, tidak ada benda setelah *punya saya*, jadi banyak yang menulis *This bag is my*. Ingat: **punya saya / milik saya / punyaku = mine**, tapi **tas saya = my bag**. Tiga jebakan lagi:
- Tanpa apostrof: **yours, hers, ours, theirs** (bukan *your's, her's*).
- Tanpa s tambahan pada **mine** (bukan *mines*), dan jangan *mine bag*.
- **yours** dipakai untuk satu orang dan untuk banyak orang (*kamu* dan *kalian*).

blocks.text: **Who is talking?** Budi and Sari point at their car and say *It's **ours***. But when **you** talk about them, it's *It's **theirs***. Same car, different speaker.

id.text: **Siapa yang bicara?** Budi dan Sari menunjuk mobil mereka dan bilang *It's **ours*** (punya kami). Tapi kalau **kamu** yang membicarakan mereka, jadinya *It's **theirs*** (punya mereka). Mobilnya sama, yang bicara beda.

blocks.explain: Nothing comes after the word (the phone is already clear), so we need mine. my needs a thing after it (my phone), and me is for after a verb (Call me).

id.explain: Tidak ada kata sesudahnya (HP-nya sudah jelas), jadi kita butuh mine. my harus diikuti benda (my phone), dan me dipakai setelah kata kerja (Call me).

material.title: Whose …? for one thing or many

blocks.text:
Ask about the owner with **Whose**. For **one** thing: **Whose + thing + is this?** For **more than one** (a *plural*): **Whose + things + are these?** If the thing is clear, you can just say **Whose is this?**

Answer with a name + 's, or with **mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs**:
- *Whose phone is this?* — *It's Rina's.* / *It's mine.*
- *Whose keys are these?* — *They're Budi's.* / *They're his.*
For more than one thing, the answer starts with **They're**, not *It's*.

id.text:
Tanyakan pemiliknya dengan **Whose**. Untuk **satu** benda: **Whose + benda + is this?** Untuk **lebih dari satu** (*plural/jamak*): **Whose + benda + are these?** Kalau bendanya sudah jelas, cukup bilang **Whose is this?**

Jawab dengan nama + 's, atau dengan **mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs**:
- *Whose phone is this?* — *It's Rina's.* / *It's mine.*
- *Whose keys are these?* — *They're Budi's.* / *They're his.*
Untuk benda yang lebih dari satu, jawabannya diawali **They're**, bukan *It's*.

rows.en: Whose phone is this? — It's Rina's.
Whose is this? — It's mine. Thanks!
rows.id: Ini punya siapa? — Punya saya. Terima kasih!

rows.en: Whose glasses are these? — They're his.
rows.note: glasses = more than one → are, they're

rows.en: Whose sandals are those? — They're Bu Ani's.
rows.id: Sandal siapa itu? — Punya Bu Ani.

blocks.text: **whose** and **who's** sound exactly the same, so listen to what comes after. **who's** = **who is**: *Who's that man?* (Siapa laki-laki itu?). **whose** asks about the owner and a thing usually comes right after it: *Whose bag is this?* Trick for writing: put **who is** in the gap. If the sentence still makes sense, write **who's**; if not, write **whose**.

id.text: **whose** dan **who's** bunyinya persis sama, jadi perhatikan kata sesudahnya. **who's** = **who is**: *Who's that man?* (Siapa laki-laki itu?). **whose** menanyakan pemilik, dan biasanya langsung diikuti benda: *Whose bag is this?* Trik saat menulis: masukkan **who is** ke tempat kosong. Kalau kalimatnya masih masuk akal, tulis **who's**; kalau tidak, tulis **whose**.

blocks.prompt: ___ keys are these? — They're Pak Joko's.
blocks.explain: We ask about the owner of the keys, so Whose. 'Who is keys are these' makes no sense, so not who's.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ keys are these? — They're Pak Joko's.
id.explain: Kita menanyakan pemilik kuncinya, jadi Whose. 'Who is keys are these' tidak masuk akal, jadi bukan who's.

id.title: Whose …? untuk satu atau banyak benda

material.title: 's or s'? One owner or more

blocks.text:
You know **'s** for one owner: *Rina's phone*. Now, what if there is **more than one owner**? Look at the word for the owner(s):
- **One owner**: add **'s** → *my sister's room* (one sister).
- **More than one**, and the word **already ends in s**: add only **'** → *my sisters' room* (two or more sisters), *my parents' house* (mother and father).
- **More than one**, but the word **doesn't end in s** (*children, people, men, women*): add **'s** → *the children's toys*.

Why no *parents's*? The word already has an s at the end, so English just puts the ' after it. And *children* is a special word for more than one (not *childs*), so it gets 's like a normal owner. Just remember these four: **children's, people's, men's, women's**.

id.text:
Kamu sudah tahu **'s** untuk satu pemilik: *Rina's phone*. Sekarang, bagaimana kalau **pemiliknya lebih dari satu**? Lihat kata pemiliknya:
- **Satu pemilik**: tambahkan **'s** → *my sister's room* (satu saudara perempuan).
- **Lebih dari satu**, dan katanya **sudah berakhiran s**: tambahkan **'** saja → *my sisters' room* (dua saudara perempuan atau lebih), *my parents' house* (ayah dan ibu).
- **Lebih dari satu**, tapi katanya **tidak berakhiran s** (*children, people, men, women*): tambahkan **'s** → *the children's toys*.

Kenapa bukan *parents's*? Katanya sudah punya s di akhir, jadi bahasa Inggris cukup menaruh ' sesudahnya. Lalu *children* adalah kata khusus untuk 'lebih dari satu' (bukan *childs*), jadi ia mendapat 's seperti pemilik biasa. Hafalkan empat ini saja: **children's, people's, men's, women's**.

rows.en: My parents' house is in Bandung.
rows.id: Rumah orang tua saya di Bandung.

rows.en: The children's toys are on the floor.

blocks.text: **You can't hear it.** *parent's, parents* and *parents'* all sound the same. When you speak, the situation tells people what you mean. When you write, the place of ' tells them: **parent's** = one parent, **parents'** = both.

id.text: **Tidak terdengar bedanya.** *parent's, parents* dan *parents'* bunyinya sama. Saat bicara, situasinya yang menjelaskan maksudmu. Saat menulis, letak tanda ' yang menjelaskan: **parent's** = satu orang tua, **parents'** = keduanya.

blocks.text: **The Indonesian trap.** *Buku teman saya* → learners say *the book of my friend*. In English the **owner comes first**: **my friend's book**. For people (and animals), use 's, not *of*. Names that end in s (*Agus, Dimas*) can take either: *Agus's car* or *Agus' car*.

id.text: **Jebakan bahasa Indonesia.** *Buku teman saya* → banyak yang bilang *the book of my friend*. Dalam bahasa Inggris **pemiliknya di depan**: **my friend's book**. Untuk orang (dan hewan), pakai 's, bukan *of*. Nama yang berakhiran s (*Agus, Dimas*) boleh dua-duanya: *Agus's car* atau *Agus' car*.

blocks.prompt: Dimas has two cousins. They share a flat in Jakarta. It's his ___ flat.
blocks.explain: Two cousins = more than one owner, and cousins already ends in s, so add only ': cousins'. cousin's means one cousin. (flat = apartment in British English.)

id.prompt: Dimas punya dua sepupu. Mereka tinggal bersama di satu flat di Jakarta. Lengkapi: It's his ___ flat.
id.explain: Dua sepupu = pemiliknya lebih dari satu, dan cousins sudah berakhiran s, jadi tambahkan ' saja: cousins'. cousin's artinya satu sepupu. (flat = apartemen; Amerika: apartment.)

id.title: 's atau s'? Satu pemilik atau lebih

blocks.text: In the kos fridge: *Whose milk is this? — It's mine. Yours is on the top shelf.* At the office: *Is this charger yours? — No, it's Pak Hasan's.* At a family event: *Whose children are those? — They're my cousin's.* And at the mall: *Excuse me, where is the men's toilet?*

id.text: Di kulkas kos: *Whose milk is this? — It's mine. Yours is on the top shelf.* Di kantor: *Is this charger yours? — No, it's Pak Hasan's.* Di acara keluarga: *Whose children are those? — They're my cousin's.* Dan di mal: *Excuse me, where is the men's toilet?*
